name: Crestline Selvedge Henley
description:
A classic three-button henley cut from ring-spun cotton-analog selvedge — the kind of shirt that looks like it was made forty years ago and might last another forty. The fabric has a slight slub texture, off-white with faint natural variation in the weave. Crestline runs it in six colors: natural, slate, iron, ox-blood, deep navy, and a greenish ochre they call 'fen.' The chest placket is clean and minimal, the rib cuffs snug without binding.

This is a Tier 2 staple — the shirt a warehouse supervisor wears under a fleece, the shirt a transit driver reaches for on a day off. It doesn't signal anything except that you're not trying to signal anything, which has its own quiet credibility. Worn soft after a dozen washes, the kind of shirt people keep for a decade.
what_it_says: Unpretentious, practical, someone who buys clothes to wear them rather than to be seen wearing them.
worn_by: older Tier 2 residents who've worn this brand for years
story_hooks: A Crestline henley found in a locker at a decommissioned rail depot still has a name tag sewn into the collar — the name matches a missing person case from eleven years ago.
Crestline recently switched manufacturers to cut costs; longtime wearers can immediately tell the new batch is wrong, and a small community of people is quietly stockpiling the old inventory.
A Tier 4 fashion house quietly bought Crestline's fabric supplier and has been slowly degrading the quality — a small act of cultural erosion nobody has noticed yet.

physical_description.visual_profile: A timeless, understated henley with a relaxed yet composed silhouette. Evokes heritage workwear and quiet confidence—the kind of garment that disappears into daily life while maintaining subtle visual presence. Minimal branding, maximum durability.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed but not oversized; tailored through the shoulders and torso with enough ease for layering or movement. Rib cuffs are snug at the wrist without compression. Length hits at the hip, suitable for tucking or wearing loose.
physical_description.primary_material: Ring-spun cotton-analog selvedge—a synthetic evolution of vintage denim construction, engineered for durability and natural aging. Breathable, warm-hand texture with heirloom-grade longevity.
physical_description.texture: Slight slub weave creates subtle surface irregularity—a soft, lived-in quality that appears intentional rather than accidental. Yarn variation visible under close inspection. Softens further with repeated wash cycles.
physical_description.color_scheme: Six colorways: natural off-white with faint weave variation, slate gray, iron charcoal, ox-blood burgundy, deep navy, and muted greenish-ochre ('fen'). All feature organic color inconsistency suggesting natural dyeing heritage.
physical_description.closures: Three-button placket at chest—matte polymer or wood-grain buttons, spaced traditionally. Clean, secure closure without ostentation.
distinctive_features: Minimal chest placket—no visible branding or chest pocket
Selvedge edge visible on interior seams—mark of quality construction
Rib knit cuffs and neckline—classic henley structure
Natural weave variation throughout—each piece subtly unique
Designed to age visibly—fading and softening are features, not flaws
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 2 functional luxury—corpo middle management and skilled labor workforce. Accessible pricing (Φ280-340 range) signals confidence without excess.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by warehouse supervisors, transit operators, maintenance techs, and corporate middle-tier workers during off-hours. Signals competence, reliability, and deliberate understatement. A uniform of people who don't need to perform wealth.
physical_description.condition_typical: Breaks in beautifully—slight fading at stress points (cuffs, collar, button area), softening after 10-15 wash cycles. Worn-in pairs show subtle color variation and pill resistance. Decade-long lifespan normalizes patina.
